intro: A temporal holdout must respect the direction of time. An embargo removes observations near the boundary so neighboring examples do not straddle the split.
task: Partition observations around a time cutoff, retaining explicit indices for the embargoed gap.
requirements: times is a finite numeric vector, possibly empty and unsorted. cutoff is a real scalar and embargo is a nonnegative real scalar.
Return integer index arrays train, test, and gap. Train uses times < cutoff-embargo; test uses times >= cutoff+embargo; gap contains everything else.
Preserve original row order and use half-open boundary conventions exactly. With zero embargo, times equal to cutoff belong to test.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Define membership masks first
hints.body: Compute train and test masks independently using the stated strict and non-strict inequalities.

hints.title: The gap is the complement
hints.body: Every row must belong to exactly one of the three returned index sets.

explanation: A temporal split tests predictions on later observations. The embargo discards a band around the cutoff, which can reduce overlap between temporally adjacent examples.
The exact inequalities matter: the lower embargo boundary belongs to the gap, while the upper boundary belongs to test. This convention yields disjoint and exhaustive row sets.
